content.text:
Yes. In the installed agents 0.27.0, `createMcpHandler` (exported from `agents/mcp`) serves an `McpServer` from `@modelcontextprotocol/server` v2. The catch is that you have to pass a factory function, not a server instance.

The parameter type is v2's own `McpServerFactory`, which is `(ctx: McpRequestContext) => McpServer | Server | Promise<McpServer | Server>` (`node_modules/agents/dist/handler-stateless-DxYpJ_XF.d.ts:87`). The handler calls that factory for every request, so concurrent requests each get their own server. A single `McpServer` instance created up front won't type-check. Write `createMcpHandler(() => { const server = new McpServer(...); /* register tools */ return server; })` instead.

I checked this against the type definitions only; I didn't run anything.
